<Rep. Rosa L. DeLauro, Rep. Sanford D. Bishop, Jr.>: This is not a bill we can support.
We do note that it is much better than the bill considered in full committee last year, but not enough better to merit our support.
It fails to provide the full fruit and vegetable voucher level for participants in WIC recommended by the National Academies of Science, Engineering and Medicine.
How this is consistent with the administration's efforts to increase the consumption of fruits and vegetables escapes us.
It is also $200 million below last year's WIC funding level at a time when rising food costs may mean significantly higher funding will be needed.
Further, the bill did not include language allowing virtual certification for WIC participants. For mothers in rural and other remote areas having a virtual process is crucial.
During today's markup, Democrats were successful in passing Ranking Member DeLauro's proposal requiring FDA to conduct a study on infant formula safety and testing protocols for domestic and foreign formula manufacturers.
Commendably, the bill funds rural housing programs at the 2026 level, but it fails to do the same for rural water and waste grants and water and waste funding for Colonias, Alaska, and Hawaii.
Commendably, the bill funds the McGovern-Dole Food for Education Program at the 2026 level, but it cuts funding for the Food for Peace program by 25%, hurting both farmers and hungry people around the world.
One of the biggest threats to our farmers and rural communities are the bill's cuts to Farm Service Agency, Natural Resources Conservation Service, and Rural Development staffing levels. After DOGE and administration policies savaged staff levels, the administration has reversed course and is beginning to hire. These levels would make that difficult or impossible and mean that farmers and rural citizens will have to wait longer for assistance at these offices and travel farther.
We are not happy with funding cuts to the Food and Drug Administration and the bill's utter failure to address the bizarre and unscientific policies the administration has advanced on vaccines and other critical products.
It contains ``culture war'' riders that are unacceptable and would also eliminate protections for small meat and poultry producers, a gift to large corporations. We join the American Farm Bureau Federation in opposition to this.
We look forward to improving the bill as the legislative process continues.
Rosa DeLauro.
Sanford D. Bishop, Jr.
